title: Fly into the Kalash valleys of Chitral
credits: 3D terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: High in the Hindu Kush, in Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, live the Kalash people.
Let's fly up the Chitral River, towards three small valleys that are home to one of Pakistan's smallest communities.
Here, a side valley opens to the west.
This is Bumburet, the largest of the three Kalash valleys.
The Kalash number only a few thousand people, about four thousand by one estimate.
They have their own language, Kalasha, and their own ancient religion and traditions.
Kalash women are known for their black dresses, embroidered with bright colours, and their elaborate headdresses.
To the north lies the Rumbur valley.
Every May, the valleys welcome spring with the Chilam Joshi festival: three days of music, circle dances, and prayers for the fields and animals.
To the south is Birir. In winter, all three valleys celebrate Chawmos, their grand new year festival, for about two weeks.
Scholars still debate where the Kalash came from, and UNESCO has considered their culture for World Heritage listing.
